items.followUp: Why is air considered a mixture while carbon dioxide is a compound?

rubric.why: A mixture can have varying proportions, and its components are physically mixed.
rubric.description: Gives a distinguishing feature of a mixture, such as variable composition or physical mixing.

rubric.why: Water is a compound whose elements are chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
rubric.description: States that hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed ratio, or gives the formula H₂O.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the fixed-ratio combination or correct formula.

modelAnswer: A soft drink is a mixture because its components are physically mixed and its composition can vary.
Water is a compound because hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed ratio (H₂O).

items.followUp: State the modern periodic law and identify the property on which the modern Periodic Table is based.

rubric.why: The law states that elemental properties recur periodically.
rubric.description: States that the properties of elements are periodic functions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the periodic nature of the properties.

rubric.why: The modern periodic law relates this periodicity to atomic number.
rubric.description: States that the periodic functions are of the elements’ atomic numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying atomic number as the basis.

modelAnswer: The properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

items.followUp: How do atoms form an ionic bond to attain a stable electronic configuration?

rubric.why: Atoms react to attain a more stable electronic arrangement, commonly like that of a noble gas.
rubric.description: States that atoms react to attain a stable electronic configuration or a noble-gas configuration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the stability or noble-gas configuration idea.

rubric.why: Losing, gaining, or sharing electrons can complete an atom’s outer shell.
rubric.description: Mentions completing the outermost shell or doing so by losing, gaining, or sharing electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid way of attaining the stable configuration.

modelAnswer: Atoms react with each other to attain a stable electronic configuration, usually by completing their outermost shell.
They do this by losing, gaining, or sharing electrons.

items.followUp: Define a polar covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: Equal sharing of bonding electrons is the defining feature of a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: Defines a non-polar covalent bond as one in which the bonded atoms share electrons equally.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bonding electrons are shared equally.

rubric.why: Each listed molecule has a non-polar covalent bond between identical atoms.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as H₂, Cl₂, O₂, or N₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct example.

modelAnswer: A non-polar covalent bond is a covalent bond in which the bonded atoms share the bonding electrons equally.
Examples include H₂, Cl₂, O₂, and N₂.
